scope: Native corpse reclaim packet admission and repeated requests
finding: No production defect found in the exercised handler paths. Existing WorldSession::HandleReclaimCorpse checks alive/arena/ghost state, owns corpse lookup through Player::GetCorpse, checks native reclaim delay, 3D distance and IsInMap, then resurrects and converts the corpse. This commit adds native regression coverage only.
checks: Test-CorpseRestartNative.ps1 -VerifyReleaseBinary passed: 48 new cases = 12 modes x Human/Orc x PvE/PvP death; 12 accepted, 36 rejected. Native serialized ReclaimCorpse packets are decoded by MiscPackets::Read and passed to the actual WorldSession handler from the final-link game library.

Each case executes actual KillPlayer/BuildPlayerRepop and corpse SQL save, checks dead/8326/ghost inputs, unloads cache without SQL deletion, supplies only a controlled saved time, and reloads the real corpse through ObjectMgr::LoadCorpses. Map IDs are checked before attaching the matching map pointer required by Map::AddToMap; IsInMap is asserted before testing admission.

PvE/PvP reclaim-delay configurations are enabled within the fixture and restored afterward. Actual GetCorpseReclaimDelay returns30s. Native GameTime is asserted unchanged across requests; one second early is rejected, exact delay and one second after are accepted. No private corpse time or admission result is mocked.

Horizontal100 and vertical100 offsets reject reclaim. Edge cases use native CORPSE_RECLAIM_RADIUS39 plus the actual corpse/player object sizes, with 0.25-yard margins inside/outside; only inside is accepted. These margins avoid float rounding and do not claim exact mathematical equality coverage.

Other-map1 and same-map1220/different-instance71 cases use actual distinct Map objects with the Player moved through native world/grid/map attachment components. Both assert close distance and IsInMap=false before the handler rejects. This is handler/map identity coverage, not an authenticated teleport or instance-admission test.

An unreleased-state input removes the native ghost aura and asserts no ghost flag while remaining dead. Missing-corpse input converts/deletes the corpse before the request; already-alive input invokes native resurrection before the request. All three reject without changing health or death state.

Each accepted request leaves the Player alive with500/1000 health, no8326/ghost flag and no owner-indexed corpse; a second identical decoded packet after setting health321 leaves health321 unchanged. Rejected requests retain the same corpse pointer and SQL GUID except the explicitly absent-corpse control. Actual SQL row counts verify deletion for accepted/missing cases and preservation for all other cases.

All new cases clean up before the existing independent corpse writer/reader persistence, startup/runtime expiry, missing-corpse login and GUID identity controls run. Those existing checks and the canonical Release hash/loader checks also pass. DBErrors.log is empty and Server.log contains no ERROR entries.

Native freshness dependencies now include MiscHandler.cpp, Object.cpp and MiscPackets.cpp; native-inputs hashes include the new CorpseReclaimNative.inc. No production source or migration changed, so no Release rebuild or background server startup was needed. Canonical executable and actual final-link library hashes are recorded. Schema-only temporary databases and scratch SQL user are removed by the existing wrapper.

retained_failures: .codex/corpse-reclaim-native.log: initial fixture constructed map1 before reserving it in native VMAP/MMAP bootstrap, which only listed1220. MMapManager asserted invalid mapId1. Fixture now registers both map IDs before constructing maps; no production map loader change.

.codex/corpse-reclaim-final.log and corpse-reclaim-diagnostic.log: initial SQL-hydrated corpse had IDs but no active map pointer. Map::AddToMap explicitly requires its caller to attach that pointer; IsInMap was false and exact-delay reclaim was correctly rejected. Fixture now checks restored IDs, attaches the matching map and asserts IsInMap before the request.

.codex/corpse-reclaim-attached.log: added diagnostic dereferenced a local corpse pointer after explicit missing-corpse conversion deleted it. This fixture-only diagnostic crashed. The pointer is now cleared on deletion and those diagnostics were removed. Final complete run passes all48 cases with no native errors.
limits: Socketless native Players and component map attachment are used. This does not run network opcode routing, authenticated login, aggregate Player::LoadFromDB, real client movement or the client resurrection dialog.

The fixture uses stack Map objects and creates no character rows. Owner-indexed corpse conversion and real corpse SQL deletion are asserted; bones creation/visibility and subsequent character SaveToDB results are not independently asserted. SaveToDB defaults to UPDATE, which cannot establish durable character recovery without an existing character row. No full persisted character-state or visual bones claim is made.

Arena rejection, battleground full-health resurrection, disabled delay settings, escalating delays from repeated deaths, phase visibility and transport-relative reclaim distances are not new coverage in this fixture.

The request GUID is decoded and set to the actual saved corpse GUID. The native handler intentionally looks up the requesting Player own corpse; foreign/stale GUID behavior across a subsequent death is not newly verified.
Cold-client resurrection UI, release countdown, movement, corpse/bones appearance and camera/pet state remain pending client verification. Earlier audit limitations and failures are retained.
